Hi Laura — great to hear from you. Short answer: we support both models depending on what you need (predictability vs pure unit economics). Below is a sketch with ballpark numbers to help procurement model things; happy to walk through on a call.

Option 1 — Predictable bundle (recommended for regulated apps)
- Audit logs (30-day retention): flat $4,000 / month per account (includes ingestion up to 5TB/mo, excludes long-term archival)
- KMS (customer-managed key + integrated rotation): $1,200 / month (includes key ops + HSM gateway if requested)
- Data residency (single region isolated tenancy): $3,500 / month (infrastructure and isolation premium)
- HIPAA-ready bundle: $6,000 / month (includes audit logs 90-day retention, KMS, BAA, and annual readiness review)

Option 2 — Usage-aligned uplift (better if volumes are uncertain)
- Audit logs: $0.15 / GB ingested + $0.02 / GB / month retained; estimated uplift ~6–8% on invoice depending on usage profile
- KMS/HSM: $300 provisioning + $0.05 / request over threshold; HSM hardware surcharge typically +10% of infra line item
- Residency: regional surcharge expressed as % uplift (US-East default 0%, US-West/EU +6–12%)

Discounting and commits: we can give standard volume discounts (10% for 12-mo commit, 18% for 24-mo), and a separately-negotiated enterprise credit for migration costs.

I attached a pricing workbook with example math (redwood-compliance-pricing-v3.xlsx). If you want, I can put together a mutual action plan for procurement with milestones and a recommended route (bundle vs uplift).

Would you be available Wed or Thu to review?
